elements.char: Additionally, several studies have demonstrated that small pulmonary arteries become smaller and shrink at subsegmental
elements.label: text

elements.char: levels in patients with COPD [
elements.label: text

elements.char: ], and endothelial dysfunction may be caused by both pulmonary and extra-pulmonary
elements.label: text

elements.char: vascular alterations in COPD [
elements.label: text

elements.char: ]. Therefore, having an automated method for airway and vessel morphology
elements.label: text

elements.char: assessment will help precise measurements of the geometrical properties of bronchial and venous trees which, in turn,
elements.label: text

elements.char: may lead to improved diagnosis and open the door to new studies on lung disorders.
elements.label: text

elements.char: While in the past several methods have been proposed with the aim of helping physicians accurately locate small
elements.label: text

elements.char: pulmonary airways and veins on chest CT images [
elements.label: text

elements.char: ], up to date not much work has been proposed for sub-voxel
elements.label: text

elements.char: morphology assessment. Traditional approaches for airway wall thickness detection are based on edge-detection
elements.label: text

elements.char: methods, that, although limited by the Nyquist theorem, use the reconstructed CT signal to analyze properties of the
elements.label: text

elements.char: structure directly. Among them, the full width at half max (FWHM) [
elements.label: text

elements.char: ], for which the true edge of an ideal step
elements.label: text

elements.char: function undergoing low-pass filtering is located at the FWHM location, is one of the most typical algorithms. In [
elements.label: text

elements.char: a modified FWHM, as proposed in [
elements.label: text

elements.char: ] is used as available in the Virtual Bronchoscopy program (Siemens Medical
elements.label: text

elements.char: Solution), to determine the effect of bronchodilation on airway metrics derived from airway wall thickness reflecting
elements.label: text

elements.char: airway disease in patients with COPD.
elements.label: text

elements.char: The main drawback of the FWHM method is that if the airway wall is considered as a laminated structure whose scale
elements.label: text

elements.char: is close to the scanner scale resolution, the edge principle the FWHM is based on would be violated. Therefore, as
elements.label: text

elements.char: reported in [
elements.label: text

elements.char: ], the measurements provided by FWHM are biased towards under- or over-estimation of the inner or
elements.label: text

elements.char: outer boundary, respectively. For this reason, in [
elements.label: text

elements.char: ] a model-based fitting method, assuming a Gaussian point spread
elements.label: text

elements.char: function (PSF) and an idealized step-like model for the airway, was proposed. However, this method is computationally
elements.label: text

elements.char: very expensive and does not take into account deviations from the proposed model, such as areas where the airway wall
elements.label: text

elements.char: is in contact with a vessel.
elements.label: text

elements.char: Another popular approach to measure airway walls involves the use of the zero crossings of the second order derivative
elements.label: text

elements.char: (ZCSD) and the phase congruency of the local phase [
elements.label: text

elements.char: ], which characterizes lumen-to-wall and wall-to-
elements.label: text

elements.char: parenchyma transitions. While shown to provide better localization of the airway wall than FWHM and to be less
elements.label: text

elements.char: sensitive to different reconstruction kernels and radiation doses, this technique is still computationally expensive and, as
elements.label: text

elements.char: admitted by the authors, still sensitive to overestimation.
elements.label: text

elements.char: A method based on 2D dynamic programming approaches was also proposed to detect both the inner and outer
elements.label: text

elements.char: boundaries in cross-sectional images, utilizing cost functions combining the first and second derivatives [
elements.label: text

elements.char: ]. However,
elements.label: text

elements.char: validation was perfomed only on phantom CT images and in-vivo results were not provided.
elements.label: text

elements.char: More recently, a new algorithm for airway wall segmentation that combines coarse airway segmentation and optimal
elements.label: text

elements.char: graph construction was proposed [
elements.label: text

elements.char: ]. Comparison to manual annotation and correlation of Inner Volume (IV) and Wall
elements.label: text

elements.char: Volume Percentage (WV%) with predicted forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1%) were used to validate
elements.label: text

elements.char: the method. However, the proposed technique requires a complex and time consuming parameter tuning and it still
elements.label: text

elements.char: computationally expensive. Moreover, no comparison with FWHM and ZCSD is provided. A similar approach was
elements.label: text

elements.char: also proposed in [
elements.label: text

elements.char: ], where a more accurate validation was presented. Nevertheless, as claimed by the authors, the
elements.label: text

elements.char: suggested technique may not always be achievable as it requires the pre-segmentation step to define complete airway
elements.label: text

elements.char: trees, which is not always feasible.
elements.label: text

elements.char: While different methods have been proposed in the literature for measuring airway wall thickness and lumen, just a few
elements.label: text

elements.char: studies have tried to accurately measure the vessels radius with high precision, making the proposed technique very
elements.label: text

elements.char: relevant in the field. Some approaches are mainly based on edge detectors and the relation between scale and physical
elements.label: text

elements.char: radius based on an idealized Gaussian model for vessels [
elements.label: text

elements.char: ]. In a recent work, a technique for vascular morphology
elements.label: text

elements.char: quantification based on FWHM was also proposed [
elements.label: text

elements.char: ]. However, the method uses the centerline and its distance to the
elements.label: text

elements.char: vessel border (previously segmented) to compute the vessel radius. While acceptable for big vessels, this method is
elements.label: text

elements.char: prone to high errors for peripheral vessels. Also, no validation of the vessel morphology quantification is provided.
elements.label: text

elements.char: The main drawback of all traditional methods is that they suffer from over- and under-estimation errors, especially for
elements.label: text

elements.char: small stuctures at the scanning resolution [15].
elements.label: text

elements.char: To overcome these issues when measuring small airways and vessels, we propose the development of a convolutional
elements.label: text

elements.char: neural regressor (CNR) [
elements.label: text

elements.char: ], that accurately learns the main characteristics of the structures and automatically regresses
elements.label: text

elements.char: the airway wall thickness, airway lumen, and vessel radius regradless of the parameters used for CT acquisition. This
elements.label: text

elements.char: is accomplished by using small 2D patches extracted on the orthogonal plane along the main axis of the structure of
elements.label: text

elements.char: interest.
